title: Priests Mind Control

sources.label: How To Play ★★★ PRIESTS In Dota Auto Chess

body:
# Priests Mind Control

This is a gimmick board that wins by using the enemy's own units against them.
The 4-Priest bond makes every Priest mind-control an enemy unit at the start of
each round — and the number you steal equals *your board capacity minus the
pieces you have deployed*. So the entire build is about running fewer units than
your level allows: a nearly empty board of high-level Priests hijacks the
opponent's strongest, best-itemized units and turns them loose on their former
team. Priests themselves are immune to mind control, so this doesn't happen back
to you. It's deliberately weak until it comes online — you spend the early game
losing on purpose and hidden — but once assembled it feels almost unfair.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chen | 4 | Orc, Priest | The centerpiece — highest-level Priest, holds Witless Shako, and revives kills |
| Shadow Demon | 1 | Demon, Draenei, Priest | Cheap Priest; a three-star Shadow Demon controls three-star tier-four targets |
| Oracle | 2 | God, Priest | Priest body with survivability utility |
| Dazzle | 1 | Priest, Troll | Cheap Priest; a three-star Dazzle keeps the team alive with Shadow Grave |
| Luna | 2 | Elf, Knight | The lone damage dealer — your stolen units tank while Luna does the killing |
| Troll Warlord | 5 | Troll, Warrior | Optional frontline body to soak damage while the steals go to work |

The four Priests (Chen, Shadow Demon, Oracle, Dazzle) are the whole engine; Luna
provides the raw damage that Priests alone can't, and any extra bodies exist only
to survive. Because control count scales with empty board slots, resist the urge
to fill the board.

## Items

The signature item is **Witless Shako** — a tier-one neutral that grants +1
monster level, which lets a Priest mind-control a target one tier *above* its own
level. Put it on your highest-level Priest (usually Chen) so you can steal
tier-four units, two-star legendaries, and even neutral monsters. Every offensive
item goes on Luna (**Daedalus**, **Satanic** for lifesteal), since she's your
only real damage source. Everything else is survival: put defensive items on the
frontline body so your Priests live long enough for the controlled units to win
the fight.

## Relics

Nothing build-defining here — prioritize the losing-streak economy relics
(Malefic Rapture, Magic Seed) that fund the slow climb, plus anything that boosts
survivability. Spend IO on Chen when you find it, since a higher-level Chen
controls higher-tier units. The double-sided talent at round 15 is worth taking
for the level bump on Chen plus the roll discount and reduced health loss.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Open fort and lose on purpose from round 4 onward, selling down to only Priests
(plus Luna) to hit 40 gold fast — the 2-Priest bond hands you a Tango every home
loss (as long as your board is under capacity), so you stay resilient even at low
HP. Ban units to raise your odds of finding Chen (the video bans Beast, Sand
King, Lone Druid, and Monkey King), and if Chen is slow to appear, two Wizards
can temporarily stand in for the Priest count. Reveal the build as late as
possible — ideally after round 20 — so opponents don't have time to roll
Gossamer Cape against you. Prioritize three-star Oracle and Shadow Demon plus at
least a two-star Chen; the higher your Priests' star level, the higher the tier
of units you can steal.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Spread your Priests out rather than clumping them — the one hard counter is Riki's
smoke cloud, which silences your Priests for the first few seconds and stops them
from casting mind control, so keep your key Priests (Chen, Shadow Demon) on the
flanks out of the cloud. Knights are your favorite matchup: they field few units,
so stealing their Chaos Knight and Luna simply ends the fight. Watch for a few
snags — **Gossamer Cape** on an enemy's best unit blocks the steal (though you can
usually take their second- or third-best instead), transformation units like
Dragon Knight and Lycan revert to their owner after transforming, and a
high-level enemy dragon on the neutral round can't be controlled without both
Witless Shako and a high-star Priest, so that's a round you'll often lose. The
build's resilience — Tango sustain plus Chen and Dazzle revives — is what lets it
grind from the bottom of the lobby to top three.
